s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with associated symptoms and signs of cardiac involvement
salient_findings: Sudden, pressure-like, substernal chest pain radiating to the left jaw
New onset of fever and worsening chest pain after intervention
Pericardial friction rub on follow-up examination
key_facts: Patient is a 52-year-old man
Chest pain started at rest and was associated with nausea, dyspnea, and diaphoresis
Symptoms began approximately 6 hours before arrival
Patient was tachycardic on initial examination
No murmurs or crackles were present on initial examination
Jugular venous pressure was normal
Initial troponin levels were 14 µg/L
Initial ECG showed ST-segment elevations in leads II, aVF, and V3-V5
Coronary angiography showed acute thrombotic total occlusion of the mid-segment of the left anterior descending artery
Ejection fraction was 55% to 60% on ventriculography and transthoracic echocardiogram
Pericardial friction rub was present on follow-up examination
Temperature was 38.3°C on follow-up examination

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with sudden chest pain, nausea, dyspnea, and diaphoresis, and had elevated troponin levels and ST-segment elevations on ECG, indicating myocardial infarction

shortlist.label: Myopericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient developed a pericardial friction rub and had diffuse ST-segment elevation on ECG, suggesting myocardial and pericardial involvement

shortlist.label: Pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had a pericardial friction rub and PR-segment depression on ECG, indicating pericardial inflammation

shortlist.label: Acute coronary syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had acute thrombotic total occlusion of the left anterior descending artery on coronary angiography, indicating an acute coronary event

shortlist.label: Post-myocardial infarction syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had a recent myocardial infarction and developed fever, worsening chest pain, and a pericardial friction rub, suggesting a post-infarction syndrome
